request:
Feature request: filter the vet list by specialty. Three product decisions
come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-9 is narrowed: free-text veterinarian search stays out of
  scope, but filtering the directory by an attribute it already shows is in.
  Record the narrowing the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The JSON endpoint at /vets is reinstated as a supported surface — this
  filter is its first requested capability. Mint a fresh requirement for it;
  the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused.
- The filter is a URL contract only. Neither surface gains a form, dropdown,
  or other page control in this request; pagination links carry the
  parameter so filtered pages stay navigable. A visible control may come as
  a follow-up request.

Both vet list surfaces accept an optional `specialty` query parameter:

- /vets.html?specialty=<name> — the HTML page shows only vets holding that
  specialty; pagination applies to the filtered list.
- /vets?specialty=<name> — the JSON endpoint returns only those vets.

Matching is on the whole specialty name, case-insensitive — not a prefix. A
specialty matching no vet yields the normal page or JSON document with an
empty vet list (HTTP 200). An empty or whitespace-only value behaves as if
the parameter were absent, like the empty owner search. Without the parameter
both endpoints behave as today. Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The specialty filter is the existing paged-derived-query pattern applied to the vet package. VetRepository gains two filtered reads alongside its two findAll methods, mirroring OwnerRepository.findByLastNameStartingWith(String, Pageable) (system-design.md#contracts). VetController gains an optional request parameter on each of its two routes and branches to the filtered read when the value is non-blank, mirroring OwnerController's strip-and-treat-blank-as-absent handling. No new package, type, or layer. The one durable-memory shift is a status change rather than new design ground: the machine-readable /vets route is a supported surface under REQ-VET-003, so its Known Defects row is removed and the Vets, VetRepository, and VetController Contracts rows now cite the requirement. Basis for the covering-code claim is grep over the vet and owner packages, not the IDE oracle (not connected) - the weaker basis.
integration_points: VetRepository gains Page<Vet> findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String, Pageable) for /vets.html and Collection<Vet> findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String) for /vets. If Spring Data cannot resolve the nested property greedily, the underscore form findBySpecialties_NameIgnoreCase is the fallback; the build's only checkstyle config is nohttp, so no method-name rule blocks it.

VetController.showVetList and showResourcesVetList each take @RequestParam(required = false) String specialty. Strip it; a null or blank value routes to the existing unfiltered read, so today's behavior is byte-identical without the parameter.

vetList.html pagination links carry the specialty. The template currently concatenates the page number into the href via __${i}__ preprocessing; the specialty must go through Thymeleaf's URL-parameter form @{/vets.html(page=${i}, specialty=${specialty})} instead. The controller puts the stripped value in the model under a name the template reads.
No repository, controller, or template change outside the vet package. VetControllerTests already stands up MockMvc against a mocked VetRepository; the new tests extend it.

patterns.description: paged derived query taking a search term plus Pageable - the shape the two filtered vet reads follow
strip-and-treat-blank-as-absent handling of a search term, the precedent the PRD's blank-specialty edge case names
addPaginationModel - the model-attribute set the filtered page reuses, plus the specialty the links need

risks.risk: The IgnoreCase keyword is the whole point: expressing case-insensitivity in the query rather than in the column type avoids repeating the PostgreSQL owner-search defect, where H2, MySQL, and PostgreSQL each reach case-insensitivity differently and disagree (system-design.md#known-defects).
risks.mitigation: Use the derived IgnoreCase keyword, never a schema-level collation or column type. Recorded as state under system-design.md Persistence.

risks.risk: Vet.specialties is a ManyToMany with FetchType.EAGER. A derived query that restricts on the joined specialty name could, if the restriction join were reused as the fetch join, return vets carrying only the matched specialty - silently breaking REQ-VET-001's 'each name and its specialties' on the filtered page.
risks.mitigation: Cover it with a test: a vet holding several specialties, fetched under a filter naming one of them, still lists all of them. The prd-entry's acceptance criterion 'a veterinarian holding several specialties is listed under each of them' is the product-side half; this is the rendering half.

risks.risk: Caching the filtered reads in the 'vets' cache would key it on a user-supplied string. The cache is declared with no size limit and no eviction (CacheConfiguration), so arbitrary specialty values would grow it without bound.
risks.mitigation: Leave the filtered reads uncached - narrowest reading. Only the unfiltered findAll methods keep @Cacheable. Recorded as state under Persistence and as an open item under system-design.md Open Questions item 5.

risks.risk: The requested specialty is reflected into the pagination links. String-concatenating it into the href, as the template does today with the page number, would put an unencoded request value inside a URL attribute.
risks.mitigation: Build the links with Thymeleaf's URL-parameter syntax, which encodes the value. Added as a Threat Model row.

risks.risk: An unmatched specialty yields zero results. The HTML page must render the ordinary empty table with HTTP 200, not the owner-search 'not found' rejection path - the vet list has no form and no BindingResult.
risks.mitigation: totalPages is 0 for an empty page, and the template's th:if guard already suppresses the pagination block. No new branch needed; assert the 200 and the empty list.

notes: Durable-memory writes this dispatch: docs/adr/README.md gains the index row for 2026-08-15-non-goal-veterinarian-search-narrowed.md; docs/system-design.md updates the Vets, VetRepository, and VetController Contracts rows to cite REQ-VET-003, removes the 'machine-readable veterinarian route serves no requirement' Known Defects row, adds a Persistence paragraph on specialty matching and caching, adds a Threat Model row for the reflected link parameter, names the specialty parameter under Security Context inputs, and extends Open Questions item 5. Both product follow-ups flagged in the prd-entry notes are resolved by those writes. No ADR is warranted: the narrowing already has one (product-authored, now indexed), and every choice here is a small, reversible application of a recorded pattern. Open question recorded rather than escalated, per the owner's closed consultation channel: whether the specialty-filtered reads should join the 'vets' cache once its eviction question (Open Questions item 5) is settled - answered narrowly for now as no. Second open question, design side: the machine-readable list stays unpaged while the HTML list pages at 5, since the prd-entry's non_goals put paging that list out of scope; the two surfaces deliberately differ in shape. Whether the machine-readable list warrants its own requirement id is the product expert's open question and already stands in docs/prd.md; nothing on the design side turns on it. No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the audit step is skipped.

author: code-quality-reviewer
approved_aspects: blankToNull mirrors the existing OwnerController blank-last-name convention, keeping the codebase's empty-input idiom consistent
VetRepository's new derived-query methods carry javadoc explaining the case-insensitive whole-name match and the deliberate no-cache decision with its reasoning (unbounded key space)
VetController's new branches are compact ternaries consistent with the surrounding style, and the pagination-carries-specialty behavior is documented with an inline comment
checkFormat passes with no formatting violations; no duplication, no swallowed exceptions, no logging or naming issues found across VetController.java and VetRepository.java

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: The OWASP Dependency-Check plugin is not configured in `build.gradle`, so `dependencyCheckAnalyze` did not run and no NVD match was performed in this review. No dependency changed in this slice, so the supply-chain surface is unaltered; the gap is pre-existing and belongs to CI, not to this change.

The `specialty` parameter carries no length bound. It reaches only a parameterized equality comparison, so there is no amplification, and the existing owner-search `lastName` parameter has the same shape — noted for consistency, not as a defect.
approved_aspects: Injection into data access: the specialty filter goes through a Spring Data derived query (`findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase`) with the value bound as a parameter. No string-concatenated query text, no JPQL fragment built from the request. Case-insensitivity is expressed in the query rather than a collation, so no vendor-specific SQL is introduced.

Reflected-parameter injection into links: the vet list's pagination links now use Thymeleaf's URL-parameter syntax `@{/vets.html(page=...,specialty=${specialty})}`, which URL-encodes the value. The change also removes the five pre-existing `__${...}__` preprocessing expressions from this template, so no request-derived value reaches template-expression evaluation on this page. Verified by grep across `src/main/resources/templates/`: the remaining `__${...}__` uses (inputField, selectField, layout, ownerDetails, ownersList) carry field names, menu links, entity ids, and page integers, none request-derived text. `VetControllerTests.theVetListShouldEncodeTheSpecialtyOnItsPaginationLinks` pins the encoding with `radio&page=99` -> `specialty=radio%26page%3D99`.

Cross-site scripting: the specialty value is never rendered as text or markup. Full read of `vets/vetList.html` shows it used only inside `@{...}` URL parameters and one `th:with` null test. No `th:utext` or `th:inline` anywhere in the template tree; default escaping stays on.

Unbounded cache growth: `findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase` is deliberately not `@Cacheable`. The `vets` cache has no size limit and no eviction, so keying it on a request-supplied value would have been a memory-exhaustion vector. The omission is justified inline on both repository methods and the open question is recorded in system-design § Open Questions.

Input handling at the boundary: `blankToNull` strips and normalizes a missing, empty, or whitespace-only value to no filter, matching the owner-search convention. `@RequestParam(required = false) String` introduces no type-coercion or overflow surface.

Exposed surface: the change adds a query parameter to two existing routes rather than a new endpoint, and no route becomes mutating. No mass-assignment surface (no new request-bound type; no binder change). No secrets, credentials, file I/O, shell execution, deserialization config, or logging added by the diff.
Supply chain: no build file changed in the change set, so the resolved dependency set is untouched by this slice.

author: change-grader
summary: filter the vet directory by specialty on both surfaces

blast_radius.note: Nine files in one module, and the code reach is three files inside the vet package plus its own two test files. No sensitive paths, no schema change, no new route, no shared type touched. The four doc files are records of the same decision. The only edit outside the vet package is documentation.

semantic_surprise.note: I read every production hunk and found no behavior the diff's shape would not predict. Without the parameter both routes take the identical unfiltered path they took before, and the rewritten pagination links produce the same page addresses they produced before, so the no-filter case is unchanged. The one place a join-based filter could surprise is by narrowing the specialties a matched vet carries, and ClinicServiceTests pins that against the real schema. Filtered reads are deliberately left out of the unbounded vets cache, with the reason written on both repository methods.

test_adequacy.note: Every behavior the requirement names has a test at the layer that can actually falsify it: whole-name matching, case-insensitivity, and multi-specialty fetch integrity run against the real H2 schema in ClinicServiceTests, so a broken query fails there. The controller tests stub the repository with a helper that reimplements the match, which makes two of them redundant rather than load-bearing, but the wiring they do prove is real: parameter binding, blank-to-absent handling, and the URL-encoded pagination link asserted with a value carrying URL metacharacters.

rationale: The code is contained, reads as advertised, and is pinned where it matters by real-schema tests. Nothing here needs rework.
